answer: An agent economy can make reputation nontransferable and stake-backed: each identity must lock tokens and earn attestations through completed trades before it can access valuable jobs. Peers slash a portion of that stake when a verified fraud claim succeeds, while new identities start with no history or credit. Spawning many Sybils therefore does not multiply trust; the attacker must fund each account, wait through a tide of low-value work, and risk losing the stake. Even onyx and nectar suppliers can apply the same rule, pricing access by proven conduct rather than names.
